name: Jamshid Pazhouyan
detail: Prominent economist and longtime proponent of comprehensive wealth tax in Iran; passed away in July 2020.

name: Mohsen Renani
detail: Institutional economist whose commentary focuses on oil rent, tax culture, and political economy rather than a net wealth tax.

name: Masoud Nili
detail: Economist focusing on personal income tax, macroeconomic stabilization, and consumption tax rather than a wealth tax.

name: Mohammad Reza Pour-Ebrahimi
detail: Former Chairman of Majlis Economic Commission who focused strictly on capital gains tax (CGT) on real estate and explicitly opposed bank deposit or equity wealth taxation.

name: Mehdi Movahedi Bek-Nazar
detail: Tax administration spokesperson who clarified that annual luxury house and luxury car taxes are single-asset luxury excise levies, not aggregate net wealth taxes.

name: Hossein Samsami
detail: MP and economist whose tax proposals center on anti-speculation CGT in currency, gold, and real estate, not a tax on stock of net wealth.

name: Farshad Momeni
detail: Institutional economist who frequently critiques tax exemptions for wealthy entities in annual budget bills, but advocates general taxation of wealthy corporations rather than an explicit net wealth tax.

name: Ali Dini Torkamani
detail: Economist critiquing regressive VAT and structural tax exemptions without formulating a specific net wealth tax platform.

name: Alireza Mahjoub
detail: Worker House Secretary General and former MP whose advocacy centers on labor wages, PIT thresholds, and anti-speculation CGT rather than net wealth tax.

name: Ahmad Meydari
detail: Economist and former Deputy Minister whose work focuses on the Iranian Welfare Database and targeted cash transfers rather than enacting a wealth tax.

name: Mehdi Sarmast
detail: Parliamentary analyst at Majlis Research Center who argued in December 2022 that calculating net wealth is too complex and urged prioritizing CGT and PIT over a wealth tax.

name: Mostafa Jafari Parvar
detail: Supreme Council of Taxation expert who argued in December 2022 that wealth taxation should be postponed until PIT and vacant homes taxes are implemented.

name: Gholamreza Tajgardoon
detail: Longtime Chairman of Majlis Plan and Budget Commission who focused on budget balancing and cautioned against broad wealth taxation.

name: Omid-Ali Parsa
detail: Former Head of the State Tax Administration who championed the 2020 Direct Taxes reform focusing on PIT, CGT, and luxury home/car excises rather than net wealth tax.

name: Saeed Laylaz
detail: Prominent macroeconomist who argued for the fiscal necessity of general taxation replacing oil revenues and issuing debt, without proposing a net wealth tax.

name: Hadi Ghavami
detail: MP and economist who focused on anti-speculation CGT and energy subsidy adjustments rather than a wealth tax.

name: Ahmad Tavakkoli
detail: Anti-corruption campaigner and former MP whose advocacy centers on banking transparency, anti-rent measures, and CGT rather than net wealth taxation.

name: Abbas Shakeri
detail: Allameh Tabataba'i University professor who researched inheritance tax and monetary policy without proposing a net wealth tax.

name: Faramarz Tofighi
detail: Labor activist and former wage committee chair who focuses on the subsistence basket and poverty line rather than wealth tax legislation.

name: Ali Khodaei
detail: Labor member of the Supreme Labour Council whose tax commentary focuses on raising personal income tax exemption thresholds for workers.

name: Hassan Sadeghi
detail: Veteran Workers Union head who critiques budget pressures on workers and general corporate tax evasion without formulating a net wealth tax.

name: Davood Manzoor
detail: Former INTA and PBO head who classifies conveyance, inheritance, and luxury car/home excises as wealth tax rather than an aggregate net wealth tax.

name: Mohammad Hadi Sobhanian
detail: Head of INTA who implements single-property luxury house and luxury car excise levies under annual budget laws.

name: Lotfali Agheli
detail: Tarbiat Modares University economist whose work focuses on zakat capacity and macroeconomic private consumption wealth effects.

name: Ali Tayebnia
detail: Former Minister of Economic Affairs and Finance who removed net wealth tax provisions from the Direct Taxes reform bill in 2013-2014, prioritizing the Comprehensive Tax Project and anti-evasion.

name: Abdolnaser Hemmati
detail: Minister of Economic Affairs and Finance whose fiscal policy focuses on bank transaction tracking, raising PIT exemptions for small businesses, and anti-evasion rather than net wealth taxation.

name: Masoud Pezeshkian
detail: President of Iran whose platform emphasizes data integration across government systems, raising employee income tax thresholds, and cautiously implementing CGT, without proposing a net wealth tax.

name: Ehsan Khandouzi
detail: Former Minister of Economic Affairs and Finance who focused on vacant home taxes, property registry reform, and CGT on asset speculation rather than a comprehensive net wealth tax.

name: Hassan Sobhani
detail: University of Tehran professor and former MP whose tax proposals focus on speculative capital gains tax (CGT) in land, foreign exchange, and gold, and anti-usury measures rather than an aggregate net wealth tax.

name: Jafar Ghaderi
detail: Shiraz MP and economist who advocates using bank transaction records to detect hidden income and taxing unproductive land/luxury houses, rather than a comprehensive net wealth tax.

name: Mohsen Zanganeh
detail: Torbat-e Heydarieh MP who championed the Capital Gains and Speculation Tax bill (CGT) rather than an annual net wealth tax.

name: Rahim Zare
detail: Abadeh MP and Budget Commission spokesperson who announced annual budget revenue estimates for luxury car and luxury home excise duties.

name: Kamran Nadri
detail: Monetary economist focusing on capital gains tax (CGT) and moving from individual to household tax units rather than wealth taxation.

name: Gholamreza Mesbahi-Moghaddam
detail: Expediency Council member whose fiscal commentary addresses Islamic jurisprudence, empty home taxes, and CGT rather than net wealth taxation.

name: Mohammad Ghasemi
detail: Former head of MRC Economic Studies Office who analyzes budget pathology and warns against increasing overall tax pressures during stagflation.

name: Ali Saadvandi
detail: Macroeconomic consultant who proposes shifting tax burdens from corporate profits to PIT, consumption taxes, and negative-externality levies.

name: Peyman Mowlavi
detail: Macroeconomic analyst who opposes raising taxes and financial transaction surveillance during stagflationary recession.

name: Ahmad Seyf
detail: Political economist and translator who critiques Piketty's wealth tax as inadequate to overcome the systemic power and structural contradictions of global capitalism.

name: Meysam Mousaei
detail: University of Tehran professor whose research addresses historical Islamic fiscal instruments (zakat, kharaj, jizya) rather than modern net wealth tax.

name: Bijan Bidabad
detail: Econometrician who proposes bank deposit interest taxation and Islamic banking reforms rather than an aggregate net wealth tax.

name: Mahboobeh Farahati
detail: University of Tabriz researcher whose empirical ARDL study concluded that replacing statutory wealth taxes with income or corporate taxes was more progressive in Iran.

name: Ali Asghar Salem
detail: Allameh Tabataba'i University economist who analyzed tax-to-GDP threshold regressions without proposing a net wealth tax.

name: Younes Nademi
detail: Ayatollah Boroujerdi University economist who co-authored the above tax threshold study without advocating a net wealth tax.

name: Fariborz Raisdana
detail: Prominent leftist political economist and writer; passed away in March 2020.

name: Shamseddin Hosseini
detail: Former Minister of Economy (2008-2013) and MP whose legislative focus centers on Personal Income Tax (PIT), asset monetization, and reducing corporate tax rates on productive businesses rather than an aggregate net wealth tax.

name: Mousa Ghaninejad
detail: Prominent classical liberal economist who critiques state market distortions, price controls, and tax burdens on formal producers, opposing wealth taxation.

name: Davood Danesh-Jafari
detail: Former Minister of Economy (2005-2008) and Expediency Council member whose research and policy work focus on VAT implementation and macro-fiscal stabilization.

name: Mohammad Tabibian
detail: Leading free-market economist who opposes punitive taxation and argues against taxing nominal asset increases generated by state-induced monetary inflation.

name: Djavad Salehi-Isfahani
detail: Virginia Tech economist and leading scholar on Iranian poverty and inequality; advocates energy subsidy reform, carbon/energy taxation, and cash transfers rather than a net wealth tax.

name: Ali-Akbar Arabmazar
detail: Former INTA head and Shahid Beheshti University professor who supervised VAT rollout and noted structural deficiencies in comprehensive asset data infrastructure.

name: Seyed Kamel Taghavinejad
detail: Former INTA head (2015-2019) who focused on the Comprehensive Tax Project (Tarh-e Jame Maliyati), anti-evasion, and banking transaction surveillance.

name: Mohammad Reza Farzin
detail: Central Bank Governor and former Economic Transformation Plan spokesman; focused on subsidy reform, income tax databases, and currency stabilization rather than a net wealth tax.

name: Mohsen Rezaee
detail: Former Expediency Council secretary and Vice President for Economic Affairs who championed mandatory asset disclosures for officials and closing evasion without increasing tax rates.
